prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport rejects POST requests in JSON response mode unless the Accept header lists BOTH `application/json` AND `text/event-stream`, incorrectly returning 406 for clients that only send `Accept: application/json`. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport rejects POST requests in JSON response mode unless the Accept header lists BOTH `application/json` AND `text/event-stream`, incorrectly returning 406 for clients that only send `Accept: application/json`. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs touch the exact same validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts and relax it to accept JSON-only clients, but the implementations differ in robustness. #1996 introduces a dedicated `acceptsMediaType()` helper that parses the Accept header per RFC 7231 semantics: it splits on media-range parameters, honors `q=0` to explicitly exclude a type, and matches type/subtype (including wildcard) rather than doing raw substring matching. #2046 instead uses direct `acceptHeader.includes('application/json')` / `includes('text/event-stream')` checks against the raw header string, which does not honor `q=0` exclusion and is susceptible to false-positive substring matches (e.g. a hypothetical `application/json-patch+json` value would satisfy the check). #1996's approach handles a strictly superset of the cases #2046 handles, so it should be kept and #2046 closed as a duplicate.
